question.text: What is the value of the constant 'e' used in continuous compounding of commodity futures prices?

explanation.text: The Logic: The mathematical constant e (Euler's number) = 2.71828, used in the continuous compounding formula F = S x e^(r x n) per workbook p.53. The Trap: 3.14159 is pi. 1.41421 is square root of 2. 2.30259 is ln(10). These are different mathematical constants. Note: Focus on setting up the continuous compounding formula F = S x e^(r x n) correctly with the source-stated value e = 2.71828.
